1.why: The system enforces server-side authorization on MFA endpoints by deriving the account solely from the session (required() function).

2.why: The same verification code (IDENTITY_CODE) is hardcoded and would work for any user in TEST_MODE, violating uniqueness.

3.why: Previous sessions remain valid after MFA is enabled (no explicit invalidation of old sessions in confirm() or codes()).

4.why: OTP secrets are encrypted (encrypt() function) and backup codes are stored as PBKDF2 verifiers (verifier() function).

5.why: Secrets and codes are generated using crypto.getRandomValues() (bytes() function).

6.why: Secrets, OTPs, and session tokens are never stored in browser storage or non-HttpOnly cookies (HttpOnly, Secure, SameSite cookies).

7.why: Server-side input validation is performed (e.g., email/phone format checks in signin(), code format in identity()).

8.why: Output encoding is handled via JSON.stringify() and CSP headers prevent script execution.

9.why: Redirects are restricted to '/' (hardcoded in signin() and other endpoints).

10.why: Secure headers (CSP, HSTS, X-Content-Type-Options, X-Frame-Options) are set in headers() function.

11.why: Session cookies are set with HttpOnly, Secure, and SameSite=Strict attributes (cookie() function).

12.why: OTP seeds, backup codes, and session tokens are never exposed in logs, URLs, or error output (only test values in TEST_MODE).

13.why: Verification codes (TOTP) are single-use and time-bound (30-second period in totp() function).

14.why: Rate-limiting is implemented via failure counters and lockout periods (addFail(), lock() functions).

15.why: Session identifiers are rotated on authentication (new session created in identity(), confirm()), but idle/absolute timeouts are enforced (IDLE, ABS constants). However, logout invalidates sessions (sessions.delete()).
